    Parse mixed-format spreadsheet dates to ISO character strings

    parse_dates.Rd

    Parse a vector containing mixed date representations commonly produced by Excel workbooks (Excel serial numbers, Unix timestamps in seconds, ISO dates and datetimes, Date/POSIXt objects, named-month dates in English, Spanish, or French, and numeric d/m/y or m/d/y strings) into standardized "YYYY-MM-DD" character strings without emitting coercion warnings.

    parse_dates(x, order = c("auto", "dmy", "mdy", "ymd"),
  ambiguous = c("na", "dmy", "mdy"),
  min_year = 1950L, max_year = 2035L,
  origin = "1899-12-30", partial = FALSE,
  na = c("", "-", "\u2013", "NA", "N/A", "n/a", "#N/A", ".", "NULL"))

    Arguments

    x

    character, numeric, Date, or POSIXt vector of dates

    order

    character. Component order for numeric 3-part dates such as "05/06/2018". With "auto" (the default), the function inspects all numeric 3-part dates in x and infers "dmy" if any first component exceeds 12 (and no second exceeds 12) or "mdy" if any second component exceeds 12 (and no first exceeds 12)

    ambiguous

    character. How to handle a numeric 3-part date when order = "auto" cannot resolve day/month order across x (for example, all values have both day and month <= 12 and unequal): "na" (default, return NA), "dmy", or "mdy"

    min_year

    integer. Minimum accepted year; dates outside [min_year, max_year] return NA

    max_year

    integer. Maximum accepted year

    origin

    character. Origin for Excel date serial numbers (default "1899-12-30")

    partial

    logical. If TRUE, also preserve valid "YYYY" and "YYYY-MM" strings

    na

    character vector of strings treated as missing values

    Value

    character vector of ISO dates ("YYYY-MM-DD", or "YYYY" / "YYYY-MM" when partial = TRUE), with NA for missing or unparseable entries.

    Examples

    parse_dates(c("41780", "2018-06-15", "15-Aug-18", "15/ago/2017", "25/06/2018", "05/06/2018"))
#> [1] "2014-05-21" "2018-06-15" "2018-08-15" "2017-08-15" "2018-06-25"
#> [6] "2018-06-05"
parse_dates(c("06/05/2018", "06/25/2018"))
#> [1] "2018-06-05" "2018-06-25"
parse_dates("06/11/2022", order = "dmy")
#> [1] "2022-11-06"
parse_dates("06/11/2022", order = "auto")
#> [1] NA
